summary: MSTR is a leveraged Bitcoin proxy whose value depends on BTC's network security and a persistent NAV premium. Quantum ECDSA risk is an unhedged long-term bomb because MSTR's core asset would be destroyed if BTC's cryptography fails. The 5-10y horizon makes post-quantum migration feasibility the critical uncertainty.

inputs.node: Bitcoin network security (mining hashpower, ECDSA signatures)
inputs.whyNeeded: MSTR's BTC holdings are only valuable if the Bitcoin ledger is trusted and secure
inputs.concentration: Mining is geographically concentrated in China/US (ASIC supply chain), but ECDSA is a single algorithm
inputs.fragility: Extreme: ECDSA is a single point of failure; if broken, BTC value collapses

inputs.whyNeeded: MSTR's market cap > its BTC holdings; premium is the source of leverage
inputs.concentration: Premium depends on retail/arbitrage demand; no single supplier
inputs.fragility: High: premium can vanish if BTC drops or arbitrage closes

inputs.whyNeeded: MSTR's asset value = BTC price * holdings
inputs.concentration: BTC market is global, but price driven by exchange liquidity and macro
inputs.fragility: Moderate: but quantum break would make BTC worthless

chokepoints.why: If quantum computers break ECDSA, all BTC transactions become forgeable; no backup yet on mainnet
If premium collapses, MSTR becomes a pure BTC discount play; leverage unwinds

customers.why: They are the only demand for MSTR shares; no real product customers
MSTR's BTC buying supports BTC price, but not a dependency

geographic: MSTR is US-based; BTC mining is ~50% US/China; quantum computing R&D is US/China/Europe
substitutes: Post-quantum Bitcoin (e.g., fork to ML-DSA/SLH-DSA) is the only substitute for ECDSA; migration would be chaotic

exposures.description: MSTR's entire value depends on ECDSA remaining secure; quantum break = total loss
MSTR's premium is a single point of failure; if it disappears, MSTR trades at discount
Bitcoin's post-quantum migration is unproven; NIST standards exist but adoption is slow

bearCase: Quantum computers break ECDSA within 10 years; Bitcoin fails to migrate; MSTR's BTC holdings become worthless; the NAV premium collapses; MSTR equity goes to zero.

loadBearing.assumption: a1: Quantum computers reach ECDSA-breaking scale
loadBearing.breaksIf: Quantum computing progress stalls or is slower than expected; error correction not achieved

loadBearing.assumption: a2: Bitcoin fails to migrate to post-quantum signatures
loadBearing.breaksIf: Bitcoin community successfully forks to ML-DSA/SLH-DSA before ECDSA break; or ECDSA break is gradual

loadBearing.assumption: a3: MSTR stays a leveraged BTC proxy
loadBearing.breaksIf: MSTR changes strategy (e.g., becomes software company); or premium disappears and MSTR becomes a discount vehicle

gaps: No facts on MSTR's actual quantum risk hedging; no facts on Bitcoin core dev post-quantum roadmap timeline; no facts on MSTR's premium sustainability beyond weak source.
verifyThese: Verify MSTR's current premium to NAV (is it persistent or episodic?)
Verify Bitcoin's post-quantum migration timeline (any BIPs?)
Verify quantum computing ECDSA break timeline (e.g., 2030-2035 estimates)
diminishingReturns: Stopped at ECDSA because deeper (e.g., quantum hardware supply chain) does not change MSTR's binary outcome: if ECDSA breaks, MSTR is zero regardless of hardware details.
